paper.title_en: Polarized emission, neutrino deposition and geodesic-induced quadrupole waveforms in exact Horndeski and disformal black-hole exteriors
paper.abstract_en: We study which observables retain information about the radial structure of exact black-hole exteriors when circular-orbit or shadow diagnostics are degenerate. We compare the static non-stealth seed of quartic square-root Horndeski theory and a separate constant-kinetic disformal exterior. The first metric is used in its original seed frame, not as a new disformally generated solution. The specified nonzero-hair square-root realization has a horizon-divergent scalar invariant and an exterior scalar ghost with a negative radial characteristic speed squared. For the inverse-square lapse <math altimg="si38.svg"><mrow><mi>N</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>M</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><mi>r</mi><mo linebreak="goodbreak">−</mo><mi>χ</mi><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo linebreak="goodbreak">/</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math>, we derive an exact eccentric separatrix and regular anomaly equations. At fixed turning points (8M, 24M), changing χ from zero to one lowers the radial frequency by 5.18% and raises the azimuthal frequency by 6.53%, although a different Schwarzschild orbit can match both frequencies. Fully differentiated eccentric mass quadrupoles yield distinct numerical-kludge burst profiles and, for suitable periodicity classes, a recurrence shorter than orbital closure. These are geodesic-induced quadrupole waveforms. Polarization is a source-dependent geometric response, and moving the prescribed neutrinosphere can reverse the fixed-radius deposition trend. The constant-disformal comparison preserves the critical shadow radius and azimuthal frequency while changing radial and transport observables. Published EHT and stellar-precession summaries are translated only into approximate, assumption-dependent consistency estimates. In particular, a Gaussian summary likelihood with a uniform nonnegative-χ prior gives approximate 95% upper endpoints 0.967 and 1.142 for the two Sgr A* mass–distance priors. Fixed-theory mass comparisons retain the coupling length.
